data.name: Asger
data.gender_notes: Asger is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word asghar, which means helper or supporter. In Islamic history, Asghar was the name of Imam Ali's youngest son and the Prophet Muhammad's grandson. The name Asger carries the meaning “Helper, Supporter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asger usually hope their child will grow to embody helper, supporter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carrying the weight of the world on your shoulders, providing support and guidance to those around you.
data.etymology: Asger belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helper, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asger total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Asger
in_english.meaning: A name that means a child who is very hungry or a person who is very eager
in_english.long_meaning: The name Asger is derived from the Arabic root 'as-ghar', which means to be very hungry or eager. In Islamic tradition, the name Asger is associated with the Prophet Abraham, who was also known as 'Asger' due to his intense hunger and devotion to Allah. In modern times, the name Asger is often given to children who are born with a strong appetite or to people who are known for their eagerness and determination.
